writtenAt: 2026-10-12 (before any evaluation; probed that day against the local container with self-registered customers: the API with curl, directly under /services/bank and through the pages' own /services_proxy/bank with a session cookie, and the Open New Account, Accounts Overview and Account Activity pages in a browser; every keyed defect reproduced at least twice with a control call that behaves correctly)
format: a product-owner story with nine numbered acceptance criteria, web pages and API together; the checks need a data chain: a registered customer, the first account they get on registration (the funding account), a new account opened from it, then the overview, the account details and the history of both accounts; the access criterion needs a second registered customer

defects.description: an account is opened although the funding account does not hold the minimum opening deposit, and the funding account goes below zero. API: a customer's first account holds 515.50 and the deposit is 100.00; the sixth POST /services/bank/createAccount?customerId={c}&newAccountType=1&fromAccountId={first} still answers 200 with a new account and the funding account reads -84.50 (the first five are the control: 515.50 down to 15.50). Web: Open New Account with a funding account that holds $0.00 shows "Account Opened!" and the overview then lists the funding account at -$100.00, a second time at -$200.00. The story requires a refusal with a reason and no balance change, and no account below zero

the API opens a loan account on request: POST /services/bank/createAccount?customerId={c}&newAccountType=2&fromAccountId={a} answers 200 with {"type":"LOAN"} and the account is listed for the customer with the deposit moved (reproduced for two customers; control: types 0 and 1 give CHECKING and SAVINGS, and the web page offers only those two). The story allows only checking and savings and reserves loan accounts for approved loan requests

an account type that does not exist is not refused with a reason: POST /services/bank/createAccount with newAccountType=5, 7 or -1 answers 500 with the site's HTML page "An internal error has occurred and has been logged." (no account is created; control: an unknown funding account or an unknown customer answers 400 with a plain message "Could not create new account for customer ... from account ..."). A text value such as newAccountType=SAVINGS answers 404 with an empty body. The story requires a refusal with a clear reason

the API's answer to opening an account shows the new account with "balance":0, while the account holds the opening deposit: POST /services/bank/createAccount answers {"id":N,"customerId":c,"type":"SAVINGS","balance":0}, and GET /services/bank/accounts/N and GET /services/bank/customers/{c}/accounts straight afterwards show "balance":100.00 (every opening call made during probing, more than ten; the two GETs are the control and agree with the web pages). The story requires the answer to be the new account as it stands after opening, opening balance included

a customer can fund a new account from another customer's account, and open accounts in another customer's name. Signed in as customer B (session cookie, through the pages' own /services_proxy/bank): POST createAccount?customerId={B}&newAccountType=0&fromAccountId={an account of A} answers 200, B gets a new account holding 100.00 and A's account is 100.00 lower (reproduced with two pairs of customers, also directly under /services/bank). Signed in as A: createAccount?customerId={B}&... with A's account opens an account owned by B. Control: an account number that does not exist answers 400. B can also read A's accounts: GET customers/{A}/accounts and accounts/{A's account} answer 200 with the balances under B's session. The story requires that a customer opens accounts only for themselves and only from their own accounts

the API opens accounts for anybody who is not signed in at all: POST /services/bank/createAccount?customerId={c}&newAccountType=1&fromAccountId={a} with no cookie, no header and no credentials answers 200 and moves the deposit (every direct call during probing was made this way), and GET /services/bank/customers/{c}/accounts answers 200 the same way. Control: the same calls through /services_proxy/bank without a session cookie answer 401 {"message":"User login required"}, and with the customer's session cookie 200. The story requires that nobody who is not signed in can open an account in a customer's name or use a customer's money, on the pages and in the API

traps: the API takes the account type as a number (0 checking, 1 savings); the web page's select sends the same numbers. A text name (newAccountType=SAVINGS) answers 404 with an empty body, which is a mechanics fact a test must discover, not by itself the finding of D3 (the 500 on an unknown number is)
all API parameters are query parameters on a POST with no body; without "Accept: application/json" the API answers XML; refusals are plain text (400), not JSON, even when JSON is asked for

the pages are shells that load their data with calls to /parabank/services_proxy/bank/... carrying the session cookie (401 without one); the same resources under /parabank/services/bank/... need no credentials at all. A test that only uses the proxy path without a cookie sees a correct 401 and would miss D6; a test that only uses the direct path cannot tell a signed-in call from an anonymous one

a new customer starts with one checking account holding 515.50 and the minimum opening deposit is 100.00; both are settings of this installation (the page states the deposit), so a test should read them, not assume them. Five openings empty the first account to 15.50; the sixth is the one that shows D1
leaving the account type out opens a checking account (200): the story does not say whether the type is mandatory in the API; a question for the owner, not a defect
an unknown funding account or an unknown customer is refused with 400 and a message: that is correct behaviour (the control for D3)

the opening deposit is recorded as "Funds Transfer Sent" on the funding account and "Funds Transfer Received" on the new one, both 100.00: AC-9 is met. The Account Activity page shows the entry's date one day early in a browser whose time zone is west of UTC (the API stores midnight UTC); this story states nothing about dates, so it is not a finding here

when not signed in, Accounts Overview and Open New Account answer HTTP 500 with "An internal error has occurred and has been logged." instead of a sign-in prompt: no data is shown, and the story does not say what a signed-out visitor sees, so it is at most a remark

accounts cannot be closed or deleted, and the tests must not use the admin page or the clean/initialize database functions: every run leaves its customers and accounts behind, so each run must register fresh customers with unique usernames
the tests that show D5 and D6 really move 100.00 out of another test customer's account: use customers registered for that test only, and do not assert that customer's balances in another test
the Open New Account page fills its funding-account list with a call made after the page has loaded: a test has to wait for the options before choosing one
